title: Edit Trail
user: Photographers using non-destructive RAW editors who need to find images by what was done to them—masking, denoise, crop, or specific active modules—rather than by filenames and folders.

evidence.quote_or_summary: A darktable user requests collection filters that find images with specific active modules, such as an active contrast module.
A separate darktable thread requests clearer organization around AI masking work, reinforcing that editing operations themselves become important search criteria.

recurrence: Two 2026 darktable discussions centre on locating and managing work by edit operation, not merely image metadata.
current_workaround: Remember folder locations, add ad-hoc tags, inspect history stacks one photo at a time, or export sidecars and search them manually.
incumbents_and_gap: darktable and Lightroom catalogue images; their UI makes operation-level cross-project audits difficult. A sidecar index can serve this narrow search need without becoming a photo manager.
smallest_useful_product: A local CLI plus static report that indexes XMP/sidecar edit metadata, lets users query active operations and combinations, and opens the source folder. Non-goals: RAW rendering, facial recognition, hosted photo libraries, or AI image editing.
success_measure: A photographer finds every image using a named operation in a 10,000-photo sidecar library in under 30 seconds.
monetization: one-time — the tool works on personal archives and should not require uploading private photos or catalogues.
constraints: Read sidecars and metadata only; no image upload; support schema/version variation; do not index private image pixels unless explicitly requested.
why_distinct: It indexes the edit trail as a first-class artifact rather than offering another DAM or AI culling service.
